description:
Not a map demo. A static HTML 404 error page for the demo site: a Raleway webfont link, an inline style block centering a .container at 600px, an

404

with "Page not found" copy, and a shared site header ("Mapbox Demos") and footer. No Mapbox GL JS script tag, no access token, no map container, no sources, layers, controls, or API calls of any kind. It has no value as a structural or functional reference for building a Mapbox GL JS demo; its only reusable content is the outer page chrome (header/main/footer wrapper) that some other pages in this directory share.

Airport explorer over Japan. Structurally unusual: the real demo document is nested inside a site-chrome wrapper (header/main/footer plus an HTML-escaped doctype paragraph), so a full standalone page markup sits inside <main>. Uses mapbox-gl-js v3.18.0 with the dark-v11 style centered on Tokyo at zoom 10, NavigationControl, Turf.js, shared/demo-kit.js, and a tarmac-glass.css template. Data is a local GeoJSON file (data/japan_airports_merged_categorybased_z13.geojson) of airport polygons; on load it is added as a GeoJSON source feeding two fill layers, a base layer and a highlight layer whose filter matches ['==', ['get','searchbox_name'], name]. Features are deduplicated by searchbox_name into a sorted array that populates a dropdown. Selecting an airport sets the highlight filter, computes a turf.centroid, adds a Marker with a click popup, and runs a flyTo camera animation to zoom 14 (turf.bbox + fitBounds fallback). A checkbox toggles polygon visibility via setPaintProperty on fill-opacity/fill-outline-color, clicking a polygon drives the dropdown selection, and a live zoom readout updates on move/zoom.

Airport point explorer that filters by which basemap layer each airport is most associated with. Like the other airport demos the real page is nested inside a site-chrome header/main/footer wrapper. mapbox-gl-js v3.18.0, streets-v12 style over Japan at zoom 5, NavigationControl, highway-sign.css template, a left 380px panel. Data is a local GeoJSON file (data/airports_analysis.geojson); closed airports are stripped and a 'color' property is injected per airport_type before it is added as a GeoJSON source. Two circle layers render it (base plus a highlight layer filtered on 'ident'), with circle-radius as an interpolate/linear zoom ramp and circle-color from ['get','color']. A second vector tileset source (mapbox://mapbox.mapbox-streets-v8) adds an 'aeroway' fill layer inserted beneath the points, toggled by checkbox via setLayoutProperty visibility. A dropdown built dynamically with optgroups (aeroway/building/landuse/other) and per-value counts drives setFilter on important_layer, updating a statistics card. Hovering shows a hover popup with a full property table and sets the highlight filter; clicking anywhere runs queryRenderedFeatures over all layers plus a 10px box on airport-points, groups results by source layer and renders a collapsible <details> inspector popup. Streets/Satellite buttons call setStyle and re-add layers on style.load.

OpenStreetMap-derived airport boundary explorer for Japan, nested inside the same site-chrome wrapper as the other airport demos. Uses mapbox-gl-js v3.18.0 on satellite-streets-v12 at zoom 5.5, NavigationControl, Turf.js, highway-sign.css, and a 380px left panel. Data is a local GeoJSON file (data/japan-airports-osm.geojson); each feature is post-processed to derive an isMilitary flag (from military tags, operator, or Japanese name tokens like 基地/駐屯地) and an area_sqkm via turf.area. One GeoJSON source feeds six layers: civilian fill, military fill, outline line layer, highlighted fill and highlighted line (both filtered on name), and a symbol layer of airport labels. A grouped dropdown (civilian vs military optgroups, with IATA/ICAO codes) selects an airport, setting the highlight filters, adding a Marker with popup at the turf.centroid, and running a flyTo camera animation to zoom 13 with turf.bbox/fitBounds fallback. Four checkboxes toggle polygons, military, labels, and small (<1 km²) airfields via setPaintProperty/setLayoutProperty/setFilter. Statistics card, live zoom readout, Satellite/Streets setStyle switcher with a restoreLayerStates routine, and keyboard shortcuts (P/L/M/S/Escape/Space) including a Space compare toggle that hides the selected polygon against the basemap.

Not a Mapbox demo. This page loads the AMap (Gaode) JavaScript API via https://webapi.amap.com/loader.js with an _AMapSecurityConfig securityJsCode and an AMap key, then builds an AMap.Map in 3D viewMode centered on Beijing at zoom 11 with showOversea disabled. It adds a single AMap.Marker whose click opens a custom AMap.InfoWindow, an AMap.Polyline drawn from a hardcoded four-point coordinate array, the AMap.ToolBar plugin as a map control, and an auto-refreshing AMap.TileLayer.Traffic live traffic overlay at a 180 second interval. There is no mapboxgl object, no access token, no GeoJSON or vector tileset source, and no Mapbox style. Relevant only as a China-market comparison/alternative-provider reference, not as a Mapbox GL JS structural template.

Lane-level Autopilot Map API viewer over Tokyo on the dark-v11 style at zoom 16 with NavigationControl bottom-right. Structurally distinctive for implementing its own tile pipeline rather than using a vector tileset source: it converts lng/lat to slippy tile x/y/z, enumerates the tiles covering the viewport at fixed zoom 14, and fetches each from api.mapbox.com/dataservices-tiles/v1/autopilot/<layer>/{z}/{x}/{y}.geojson, accumulating features into seven empty GeoJSON sources via setData. Per-layer Maps track a tile cache, loaded-tile set and failed-tile set with 30 second retry backoff and silent 404 handling; the AUTOPILOT_TOKEN constant is intentionally blank (needs a tilesets:read secret token and a server proxy), so fetches 401 as written. Layers: lanes line layer colored by a match expression on markupColor (white/yellow), lane-groups line layer, coverage fill layer, markup-lines line layer, markup-points circle layer, markup-polygons and road-islands fill layers. UI has seven visibility checkboxes (setLayoutProperty), Load Center Tile / Load Visible Tiles / Clear All / Auto-Load toggle buttons, a status line, a live zoom indicator and a zoom<14 warning overlay. Clicking any layer opens a click popup dumping all feature properties; moveend/zoomend re-trigger auto-loading.

Side-by-side swipe comparison of two synchronized maps using the mapbox-gl-compare v0.4.0 plugin over a #comparison-container holding #before and #after divs. The before map uses the light-v11 style centered on Tokyo at zoom 15 with showTileBoundaries enabled; the after map uses the default Standard style at the same camera. Data is a local GeoJSON file (./assets/images/consolidated_buildings.geojson) of building footprints, added as a GeoJSON source in a loop over a tile-name array. It feeds a fill layer whose fill-color is an interpolate/linear ramp on a numeric property named '6_14' (blue at 0 to red at 2, coalesced to 0 when missing), filtered to features that have a landmark_name and a height greater than 20. A reusable mouseenter/mouseleave hover popup enumerates every feature property into an HTML key/value dump and changes the cursor. Map clicks log lng/lat to the console. Good reference for swipe comparison plus data-driven building choropleth.

Search Box API POI explorer with a 400px sidebar built entirely in JS. Custom Studio style over Tokyo at zoom 15 with language 'ja' and NavigationControl. A hardcoded array of 285 Japanese categories with '>'-delimited canonical_ids is parsed into a nested tree (buildNestedStructure) and rendered as an expandable, checkbox-driven category filter with per-node counts, a search box, a modal picker, and coloured chips capped at ten palette colours. Three search modes toggle the sidebar: category search calls searchbox/v1/category/<id> for each selected category with proximity and limit 10, batched 90 at a time with 1.1s inter-batch delays; suggest mode debounces searchbox/v1/suggest with a UUID session_token, an AbortController, poi_category filtering and an autocomplete dropdown, then searchbox/v1/retrieve; forward mode calls searchbox/v1/forward. Results are merged into one GeoJSON source feeding a circle layer whose circle-color reads a per-category 'color' property, with fitBounds at maxZoom 15, click popups that also scroll and flash the matching sidebar row, and hover cursor changes. A draggable pulsing HTML Marker sets the proximity centre on map click, and a style-hosted 'merchants' POI layer with its own click popup is hidden via setLayoutProperty while results are shown.

Mobile network coverage visualization over Japan rendered almost entirely by a published Studio style. Overrides the shared access token with an mbxsolutions token so it can load style mapbox://styles/mbxsolutions/cmnmsy5kw001v01rhaeol71pc, centered at zoom 4.28 with minZoom 4 / maxZoom 18; the hex-bin coverage layers live in that style, backed by the mbxsolutions.ntt-hex tileset, so the page itself adds no sources or layers. Structurally distinctive for its performance instrumentation: a performance.now() timer around the first 'idle' event reports render time in an overlay, and a self-contained FPSMeter class drives a click-to-toggle fixed FPS readout. A canvas-drawn gradient colorbar legend (createLegend) is composited with Japanese 弱い/強い end labels. A large commented-out block preserves the original interactive flow: a mapbox-gl-geocoder control restricted to JP, click and geocoder-result handlers calling the Tilequery API (api.mapbox.com/v4/<tileset>/tilequery) plus reverse Geocoding, bucketing the returned count into 標準的/良好/上品質 popup text, a jumpTo camera move, a loading overlay, and zoom-driven legend fade. Good reference for Tilequery lookups, style-hosted big-data rendering, and FPS/load-time benchmarking.

Client-side clustering of point data on the light-v11 style, centered on Tokyo at zoom 6 with minZoom 3. Data is a local GeoJSON file (data/ports.geojson) fetched on map load and added as a GeoJSON source with cluster: true, clusterMaxZoom 14 and clusterRadius 50. Three layers render it: a circle layer 'clusters' filtered to ['has','point_count'] whose circle-color and circle-radius are step expressions on point_count; a symbol layer 'cluster-count' showing point_count_abbreviated as text-field; and a symbol layer 'symbol-port' filtered to unclustered points using a custom icon registered via map.loadImage plus map.addImage, with icon-size an interpolate/linear zoom ramp and icon-allow-overlap true. Clicking a cluster runs an easeTo camera animation to the cluster centroid at current zoom + 2. Clicking an unclustered point opens a click popup rendering all feature properties as an HTML table. Paired with cluster-mts as the client-side half of a clustering comparison.

Server-side (pre-aggregated) clustering counterpart to cluster-geojson, with identical styling and camera: light-v11 style centered on Tokyo at zoom 6, minZoom 3. Instead of a GeoJSON source with cluster: true, it adds a vector tileset source built with MTS (mapbox://kenji-shima.ports-demo, source-layer 'ports') in which each feature already carries a 'count' property. Three layers consume it: a circle layer 'clusters' filtered to features where count > 1, styled with step expressions on count for circle-color and circle-radius; a symbol layer 'cluster-count' rendering the legacy '{count}' text-field token; and a symbol layer 'symbol-port' filtered to count == 1 using a custom icon loaded through map.loadImage plus map.addImage with an interpolate/linear zoom ramp on icon-size and icon-allow-overlap true. Clicking a cluster triggers an easeTo camera animation to current zoom + 2; clicking a single port logs its properties. Best reference for demonstrating tileset-side clustering versus runtime clustering.

Scrollytelling biography built on the Mapbox storytelling-template pattern: a fixed full-viewport map under a scrolling #story column, driven by the scrollama library plus an IntersectionObserver polyfill. All content lives in a single hardcoded `config` object (style mapbox://styles/mapbox/standard, projection 'globe', showMarkers, markerColor, use3dTerrain and inset flags) whose ~41 chapter objects each carry id, alignment, title, image, era/place/subtitle/narration text and a location {center, zoom, pitch, bearing, speed, curve}. Chapters render to DOM as .step cards; chapterGroup entries inject full-screen dividers and isHero entries render hero panels. Structurally distinctive: instead of calling flyTo, onStepEnter runs a custom requestAnimationFrame loop with easeInOutCubic easing that jumpTo's through a two-phase camera arc — zoom out to a globe view at zoom 1.2, then zoom back in to the chapter target — guarded by a monotonically increasing request id so stale scroll transitions abort. A single Marker is added/removed (not opacity-faded) around each flight, rotateAnimation chapters call rotateTo for a slow 30s spin, setConfigProperty sets the Standard basemap lightPreset to 'day', optional raster-dem terrain plus sky layer and an optional inset map with a viewport-bounds fill/line overlay are wired but disabled, and per-chapter onChapterEnter/Exit entries can fade any layer type via a paint-property opacity map.

Delivery territory analysis over Tokyo that assigns delivery stops to depots using isochrones. dark-v11 style at zoom 12 with language 'ja', Turf.js, tarmac-glass.css template, Japanese UI. Two local GeoJSON files (data/deliveryCenters.geojson, data/deliveries.geojson) become GeoJSON sources: centers render as a symbol layer with a custom icon loaded via loadImage/addImage, deliveries as a circle layer with an interpolate/linear zoom ramp on circle-radius and minzoom 10. A control panel offers a contour-minutes dropdown (5/10/15/20/30) and a travel-profile dropdown (walking/cycling/driving/driving-traffic) plus an analyze button. Analysis fetches one isochrone per depot through the shared fetchIsochrone helper (Isochrone API with retry/backoff), batched 50 at a time with inter-batch delays for rate limiting, then uses turf.booleanPointInPolygon and turf.distance to assign each delivery to the nearest containing depot. Results are regrouped by color into per-color GeoJSON sources with isochrone fill and line layers plus colored delivery circle layers, an unassigned grey layer, and layers/sources torn down on re-run. Hovering a depot filters its isochrone and its own deliveries into view and opens a hover popup with the delivery count.

Nearby-POI browser combining the Search Box category endpoint with the Mapbox Details API. Custom Studio style over Tokyo at zoom 11, NavigationControl, setRTLTextPlugin, map.setLanguage() for runtime labels. A Japan/US region switcher flyTo's Tokyo or New York and swaps two hardcoded category arrays (Japanese, and a 482-entry global set with a mapping table), both parsed from '>'-delimited canonical_ids into a drill-down sidebar hierarchy with breadcrumbs. Selecting a category fans out searchbox/v1/category requests for every descendant id with proximity, batched 45 per 1.1s window, deduplicated by mapbox_id into one GeoJSON source feeding four layers: a base circle layer, a selected-POI circle layer filtered on a 'selected' property, a symbol label layer using case expressions for size/colour/halo, and a camera-badge symbol layer filtered to photo_status 'confirmed' via an SVG-data-URI addImage icon. Clicking a POI or sidebar row runs a flyTo and opens a tabbed detail panel (photo gallery, basic info, contact, hours, venue attributes) built from search/details/v1/retrieve with attribute_sets basic,visit,photos,venue; an open-now status is computed client-side by checkIfOpen(), which resolves the POI's IANA timezone from its coordinates and evaluates open_hours periods including overnight spans. Structurally distinctive: every map 'idle' queues viewport POIs by distance from centre, fetches details three-at-a-time, caches them, flips badges via setData, and enables a GeoJSON export of photo-bearing POIs.

DHL-branded eight-scenario parcel-logistics capability showcase over Europe (Frankfurt→Amsterdam, Paris CDG, Cologne DC): tabbed header, a 300px side panel per scenario, and a Standard/Satellite/Light/Dark style switcher calling setStyle, with all sources and layers rebuilt on every 'style.load'. Data is hardcoded JS (shipment, milestones, telemetry, geofence polygons, 300 generated fleet points) plus two local JSON files. Scenarios cover a multi-waypoint Directions API driving-traffic route drawn as casing plus line layers with ETA and SVG-data-URI icons registered via addImage; radio-driven layer-group switching including a temperature-interpolated telemetry circle layer; two-way map/table sync where rows flyTo and setFilter a selected circle layer; clustering of the fleet GeoJSON source with step-expression cluster circles, a cluster-count symbol layer, match-colored unclustered circles, a status dropdown filtering via setData and easeTo cluster zoom; Turf.js booleanPointInPolygon geofencing against fill/line zones with a setInterval truck animation; a what3words convert-to-3wa lookup on map click with mock fallback; a requestAnimationFrame vehicle animation along a route split into driven/remaining segments via turf.lineSliceAlong and nearestPointOnLine, with optional Directions geometry, a Map Matching API line and a synchronized ApexCharts chart; and a 14-route bundle view with highlight layers, symbol-placement 'line' direction arrows from a canvas-drawn icon, and fitBounds driven by a clickable route list.

Side-by-side Mapbox Directions API vs Google Routes API v2 comparison with a Japanese UI. The Mapbox side targets custom Japan routing profiles (mapbox.tmp.valhalla-zenrin / valhalla-zenrin-premium), not standard mapbox/driving. Two independently instantiated maps, a Mapbox GL JS map on a custom Studio style and a google.maps.Map loaded dynamically from a user-supplied key kept in localStorage, kept in bidirectional camera sync by jumpTo/setOptions handlers with a zoom offset and an isSyncing re-entrancy guard. Clicking either map sets origin (A) or destination (B) per the active mode button, placing custom-element mapboxgl.Marker instances and google.maps.Marker counterparts, then fetches both APIs in parallel with a fetchId guard. The Mapbox route is rendered as a line casing layer over the full geometry plus a second line layer whose source holds per-segment LineStrings grouped by consecutive `annotations=congestion` values and colored with a match expression; Google draws Polylines colored from speedReadingIntervals. Both result panels show duration, distance and turn-by-turn steps; per-API Avoid dropdowns map to Mapbox `exclude` and Google routeModifiers. Preset routes come from swappable local GeoJSON files paired by route/role properties, resolved through Geocoding v6 when coordinates are absent, feeding a batch runner with a 400-way concurrency semaphore that streams results into a delta table and a CSV download.

Mapbox GL JS v3.19 with the Standard style, pitched and rotated over Berlin with the camera locked between minZoom 15 and maxZoom 22. Data is a single hardcoded LineString Feature in one GeoJSON source (lineMetrics true, buffer 512) feeding two layers in slot 'middle': a line layer casing, and a symbol layer whose 'symbol-placement' is 'line' so black dot icons march along the same geometry, spaced in screen pixels and therefore independent of line width. The dot icon is drawn at runtime on a 2D canvas at 128px with pixelRatio 2 and registered through map.addImage, avoiding a base64 blob and async decode. 'icon-size' and 'symbol-spacing' are zoom interpolate expressions so dots keep a roughly constant on-the-ground size; icon-allow-overlap, icon-ignore-placement are true and icon-rotation-alignment and icon-pitch-alignment are 'map' so dots stay flat and unrotated. A floating panel holds three range sliders (line width, dot size, dot spacing) that call setPaintProperty on the casing and setLayoutProperty on the symbol layer, replacing the zoom expressions with flat values. Map click logs camera state. Reference for repeating symbol markers along a route line.

Client-side label localization over streets-v12 centered on Tokyo, with no style URL change and no new tile requests. On style.load every layer's original layout 'text-field' is snapshotted into a Map keyed by layer id. An EN/JA toggle then runs a loop over map.getStyle().layers that recursively walks each text-field expression, recognizing both a bare ['get','name'] lookup and an existing coalesce-of-name shape, and rewrites it to coalesce(get name_<lang>, get name) via setLayoutProperty. Reverting to English reapplies the verbatim snapshot rather than a transform, so layers such as block-number-label round-trip losslessly. Layers whose text-field draws non-name fields (ref, house_num) are classified as skipped, with their fields summarized for display. The UI is a custom two-ended CSS switch, a four-cell stats grid (scanned, labels, rewritten, skipped) and a scrollable per-layer log built from DOM nodes; visual styling comes from the shared slate-console.css template. NavigationControl bottom-right. Contrast with language-selector, which reaches the same result through the mapbox-gl-language plugin plus setStyle instead of a hand-rolled layer loop.

Form-plus-map page for creating Mapbox User Feedback API records. The map is dark-v11 with NavigationControl, GeolocateControl, and the mapbox-gl-geocoder plugin added as a search control; note the plugin is loaded twice, v5.0.2 in head and v5.0.0 again in body. Three interchangeable location-picking methods: clicking the map drops a draggable mapboxgl.Marker whose dragend updates state; manual latitude/longitude number inputs with range validation; and navigator.geolocation with per-error-code messaging. Any pick triggers a reverse geocode against the Geocoding v5 mapbox.places endpoint to attach a place_name to the selection. A separate Feedback API token is entered in a password field, validated with a GET to api.mapbox.com/user-feedback/v1/feedback?limit=1, and cached in localStorage. The form collects a category dropdown (cannot_find, traffic_issue, road_closure_issue, incorrect_location, poi_closed, poor_routing_issue, false positive and false negative traffic, other), free-text feedback, and an arbitrary list of dynamically added name/value property rows. Submit POSTs JSON with top-level lat and lon to the feedback endpoint and surfaces the returned id or a parsed API error. Links to feedback-table.html, its read-side counterpart.

Read and browse companion to feedback-submit: a Grid.js (UMD build from unpkg) data table over the Mapbox User Feedback API, with the map in a supporting role. One persistent dark-v11 map lives in a slide-out drawer, holds a GeoJSON source plus a circle layer for the selected point, and runs a flyTo with a Popup when a row's View button is clicked; the drawer also renders id, trace id, coordinates, timestamps and custom properties. Data comes from GET user-feedback/v1/feedback with cursor pagination (after, end_cursor, has_after, plus a cursor history array backing Previous) and server-side filters assembled from the UI: free-text search, multi-select status and category filters, comma-separated feedback_id and trace_id lists, and created/received/updated before-after datetime ranges. Column visibility and order are user-configurable through a drag-and-drop modal with minimal and detailed presets persisted to localStorage. A comparison mode adds row checkboxes, collects up to four items, and renders a side-by-side field diff highlighting values that differ. Exports JSON and CSV via a shared downloadBlob helper; keyboard shortcuts for search, compare and escape.

Large last-mile delivery planner built on the Mapbox Optimization API v2 over light-v11, with jQuery and Turf.js. Roughly 7,000 of the file's lines are hardcoded arrays of New York street addresses, exposed as five selectable datasets chosen by eval() on a constructed variable name; picking one geocodes every address in throttled batches through Geocoding v6 forward, aggregates dropoffs by ADDRESS_ID, and auto-creates pickup-to-dropoff shipment lines in a GeoJSON source rendered as a black line layer plus a symbol layer of '>' glyphs at symbol-placement 'line'. Clicking a shipment opens a modal for pickup and dropoff time windows, box count, service durations and requirements (refrigeration, freeze, breakable); a vehicle modal sets routing_profile, start and end location, capacities and capabilities. Submit POSTs a version-1 locations/vehicles/shipments document then polls the returned job id until solved. Each solution route is redrawn by calling Directions (a custom Valhalla-Zenrin profile host defined in shared/demo-kit.js) with polyline6 geometry decoded by the bundled polyline helper, and a results table lists every stop with ETA and geocode timing. A post-pass runs the Tilequery API on each arrival maneuver to detect toll or motorway snapping and offers to re-solve using a nearby general_street coordinate. Japanese UI.

Simulated San Francisco to London flight played back on a globe projection, starting in satellite-v9 with a button that setStyle-swaps to Standard; all sources and layers are re-added on every style.load. Route and elevation come from Mapbox's public flightpath.json; a FlightRoute class precomputes cumulative haversine distances (helper from shared/demo-kit.js, replacing Turf) and samples position, altitude, bearing and pitch along the line. A model source loads airplane.glb and a model layer drives it: model-elevation-reference 'sea', model-translation, model-scale and per-part model-rotation, model-emissive-strength and model-opacity are all fed from feature-state updated every requestAnimationFrame, animating gear retraction, propeller spin and blur, and strobe, position and taxi lights through 'match' on ['get','part']. A line layer draws the flight path in slot 'middle'. Two camera modes: an overview fitBounds snapshot restored with easeTo, and a chase mode that rebuilds getFreeCameraOptions each frame to orbit the aircraft with lookAtPoint, suspended when raw DOM mousedown, touchstart or wheel signals a user gesture. A range input scrubs flight phase against a fabricated clock.

Address-matching demo around the Mapbox Geocoding v6 forward endpoint, scoped to New Zealand (country=nz, types=address, limit=10) and centred on Wellington. Core logic is a fuzzyGeocode wrapper: it queries the full address string first, and on zero features retries with simplified variants produced by regex strategies that strip a leading slash-separated unit number or a Unit/Apt/Apartment/# keyword prefix, recording every attempt and the discarded component as an unknown field. Results are added as plain mapboxgl.Marker instances with Popups showing feature_type, full_address, the original query and the unmatched part, and the map runs fitBounds over the marker collection with maxZoom 15. The side panel lists each result with a word-level diff that colours tokens green when they appear in the matched address and strikes them through when they do not, renders the per-feature match_code object as a list, shows words present in the query but absent from the top result, and enumerates the search attempts. Clicking a result row toggles that marker's popup. Layout uses the shared highway-sign.css template with a 380px setup panel beside the map.

Catalog landing page for the demo collection, not a map demo: it loads no Mapbox GL JS and creates no map. It fetches ./demos.json and renders a filtered list of demo entries, each row showing title, optional source hostname, external link and tag pills. Two interaction surfaces: a free-text search box matching over title, description and tags, and a category filter rendered as chips over a fixed taxonomy of Mapbox API tags (Directions API, Isochrone API, Search Box API, Geocoding API, Indoor Map Tiles, Mapbox Boundaries, Tilequery API, Optimization API, Matrix API, Vector Tiles API, Raster Array Tiles, Feedback API, MTS and others). Chip selection is multi-select with AND semantics, and each chip carries a live count of how many demos would match if that tag were added to the current selection. Colour is derived per tag from a fixed hue table expressed in OKLCH, so a tag renders identically as chip and as pill. A mousemove-tracked floating tooltip shows the hovered row's description. Dark theme, vanilla JS, innerHTML templating with HTML escaping.

Coverage-comparison tool contrasting Mapbox Boundaries polygons against Search Box API point results for 25 hardcoded Indian places. Each entry declares source 'boundaries' (with a lookup tier of pos4 or adm3, an optional csvName, and a centroid used to disambiguate duplicate names such as the several Gandhi Nagars) or 'searchbox' (with optional proximity coordinates). A boundaries entry loads a lookup JSON from data/india-<tier>.json, picks the matching record by name or nearest centroid, then adds a vector source for that record's mapbox:// tileset and a fill layer filtered with ['==', ['get','mapbox_id'], id], followed by fitBounds on the record bbox. A searchbox entry calls searchbox/v1/suggest (country=IN, limit 5, proximity when supplied, crypto.randomUUID session token), retrieves the first suggestion's mapbox_id, drops a coloured mapboxgl.Marker with a Popup, and runs flyTo at zoom 12; the session token is rotated after each retrieve. A sidebar splits places into polygon-available and point-only sections with counts, and a map badge plus header line report which path was taken. Previous layer and source are removed on every selection.

Indoor mall navigation built on third-party Mapxus indoor tiles rather than Mapbox Indoor Maps, layered over streets-v12 with Turf.js. It authenticates by POSTing an appId and secret for a token, adds a custom vector source pointing at Mapxus indoor tile URLs, and fetches the Mapxus style JSON, rewriting its layers before insertion: text-font stripped, text-field forced to ['get','name:ja'], and icon-image expressions prefixed after the Mapxus sprite sheet is fetched, sliced per icon on a canvas and registered with addImage. Floor levels are read with querySourceFeatures on the mapxus_level source layer and merged by ordinal so a shared floor across buildings becomes one button; selecting a floor rewrites every indoor layer's filter on ref:level and sets symbol-z-offset, fill-z-offset and line-z-offset, plus a fill-extrusion base plate. A clip layer plus turf.booleanIntersects hides basemap buildings overlapping the venue. Routing calls the Mapxus directions endpoint and splits the returned path into per-floor LineString segments keyed by floorId so only the active floor's route line renders, with a Japanese turn-by-turn instruction list. At init all interaction handlers (dragPan, dragRotate, keyboard, doubleClickZoom, touchZoomRotate, boxZoom) are disabled for a two-stage scripted easeTo intro and re-enabled on moveend. Venue dropdown and place typeahead for origin and destination.

Mapbox Indoor Maps showcase over 11 hardcoded Brazilian airports. Requires GL JS v3.21 and enables indoor through the map constructor's config option basemap.showIndoor on the Standard style, with the built-in mapboxgl.IndoorControl added top-right so floor levels populate automatically at zoom 16 and above. Airport chips in a collapsible glass info bar call flyTo at zoom 18, pitch 45. The structurally distinctive piece is a scripted cinematic tour: a Play/Stop button drives an async loop that flies to each airport with a raised curve value, waits for moveend, polls the DOM until IndoorControl level buttons appear, then walks floors low to high by clicking those buttons, because v3.21 exposes no programmatic floor API. Each floor dwell runs an easeTo rotating bearing 30 degrees with linear easing, with a zoom push-in on arrival, and the light preset cycles dawn/day/dusk/night per stop via setConfigProperty('basemap','lightPreset'). Cancellation uses an incrementing token checked inside a custom sleep helper. Double-click logs paste-ready center coordinates. Styling comes from the shared tarmac-glass.css and light-preset-pill templates.

Indoor airport navigation aimed at on-site mobile use, built on a custom indoor-enabled style URL (mapbox-map-design/cmjd8...) rather than Standard with showIndoor. Adds NavigationControl and a GeolocateControl configured with trackUserLocation, showUserHeading and an accuracy circle, heavily restyled in CSS with a pulsing puck. Most of the script is geolocation permission plumbing: navigator.permissions.query branching on granted, prompt and denied, a manual location button that requests a position before triggering the control, desktop auto-request versus a pulsing mobile hint, and alert-based handling per GeolocationPositionError code; the geolocate handler measures distance to each configured airport with the shared haversine helper. Six airports (SFO, LAX, HND, LHR, AMS, LAS) are hardcoded with centers, floor lists and terminal names, but the airport-picker panel is commented out, so flyToAirport writes to absent DOM nodes. Map click and mousemove run queryRenderedFeatures to surface an indoor feature's name, class and floor_level in a transient info card. On load it rewrites symbol layers' text-field to coalesce name:ja, name_ja, name, and attempts setConfigProperty indoorMapZoomThreshold inside a try/catch. CSS relocates the floor control to the left edge.

Searchable worldwide airport picker over Mapbox Indoor Maps. GL JS v3.21 with the Standard style and config basemap.showIndoor true, plus the built-in mapboxgl.IndoorControl top-right, which populates floor levels wherever the building has indoor data at zoom 16 and above. Data is a single in-memory array of roughly 190 airports (IATA code, name, lat, lng) whose coordinates were resolved once offline and baked in, so selection never issues a live geocode. The UI is a hand-rolled combobox in a glass search bar: filtering ranks IATA-code-prefix matches ahead of name-substring matches and caps results at eight, with a dropdown rendered on input, full keyboard navigation (ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Enter, Escape with scrollIntoView), mousedown-before-blur selection, a clear button, and a status readout showing the chosen airport name and code. Choosing an airport runs flyTo at zoom 16, pitch 45, duration 2500. A light preset pill (dawn/day/dusk/night) is built by the shared light-preset-pill template; styling comes from tarmac-glass.css. Unlike indoor-airport-brazil there is no camera tour, and unlike indoor-airport-gps there is no geolocation.

Japanese weather tileset explorer, the reference demo for raster-array and raster-particle layers, using d3 for color scales. A tilesets config object maps each dataset (high-resolution precipitation nowcast, past 60 minutes, short-range rain forecasts, snow depth, temperature, JMA inundation, landslide and river-flood hazard distributions, linear precipitation bands baked at several zooms, wind) to a mapbox:// url, a type of raster-array, raster-array-particle or vector, an optional style URL and an insert-above layer id. Selecting a tileset tears down all sources and layers, calls setStyle only when the style differs, fetches the tileset TileJSON to read raster_layers, bands and value range, then adds a raster layer whose raster-color is a step or interpolate expression over ['raster-value'], built either from a d3 sequential scale quantized into a selectable number of color steps or from hardcoded JMA rain, snow and hazard color tables. A time slider plus Play button steps raster-array-band across the band list; mousemove calls map.queryRasterValue for a popup value readout. Wind datasets add a raster-particle layer with sliders for particle count, speed and color. A projection dropdown switches between mercator, globe and six other projections; a legend gradient and a five-level JMA hazard meter swap in per dataset.

Label-language switcher over streets-v12 at a world-scale camera (center [30,22], zoom 1.7) with 13 selectable languages. It loads the mapbox-gl-language plugin but deliberately never passes the MapboxLanguage instance to map.addControl: registered as a control it would reapply its defaultLanguage on every style.load, including the one caused by this demo's own setStyle, snapping labels back to English. Instead the plugin's setLanguage(style, lang) is called directly on map.getStyle(), producing a style object whose label layers' text-field is coalesce(get name_<lang>, get name). A small recursive walk then post-processes that result, matching exactly that two-argument coalesce shape and inserting ['get','name_en'] as a second fallback, so a road with no translation shows Latin script rather than the local-script name. The rewritten style object is handed to map.setStyle; the vector tiles already loaded carry every name_* field, so no new tile request is involved. UI is one select plus a status line, styled with the shared slate-console.css template, and NavigationControl bottom-right. Compare dynamic-style, which reaches the same outcome by looping layers and calling setLayoutProperty itself.

Two side-by-side techniques for drawing repeating icons along a line layer, over light-v11 in Tokyo, with Turf.js. The first uses a hardcoded three-feature GeoJSON FeatureCollection carrying width and linePattern properties; its line layer sets paint 'line-pattern' to an SVG rasterized onto a canvas and registered with addImage (the markup is inlined rather than fetched, since GL JS cannot decode SVG directly and some dev servers corrupt SVG responses), a very long exponential zoom interpolate for line-width alternating between 2x and 4x the feature's width property at every integer zoom, a feature-state-driven line-opacity case, and a compound filter combining an 'in' literal test, a has/minZoom guard and a linePattern presence check. The second technique alternates two maki icons already present in the style's sprite (cafe, campsite) by splitting one LineString into equal-length chunks with turf.lineSliceAlong and setting 'line-pattern' to ['get','iconType'] per chunk; chunk length is recomputed from measured meters-per-pixel whenever zoom drifts by 0.05 so roughly one tile repeat fits each chunk. Controls are a source-buffer slider, which forces source and layer removal and re-add because buffer is a construction option, and a line-join dropdown.

Three-step e-commerce checkout to 3PL driver-handoff flow, no map layers or sources at all. Step 1 wraps a plain address form in the Mapbox Search JS mapbox-address-autofill web component (search-js v1.0.0); its retrieve event supplies structured address fields plus geographic coordinates and enables the next step. Step 2 opens a GL JS v3.8.0 streets-v12 map with NavigationControl, a draggable blue Marker, click-to-move-pin behaviour, a reset-pin flyTo camera animation, and chip buttons that toggle draggable custom-element access markers (gate, entrance, loading dock) whose dragend positions are kept in state. Step 3 assembles a Mapbox Static Images API request URL with pin-l and lettered pin-s overlays, loads that image cross-origin into a canvas to burn in a wrapped driver-notes banner and rounded order badge via toDataURL, and displays a token-redacted URL plus the JSON payload sent to the 3PL. Uses demo-kit haversineDistanceMeters to report how far the customer moved the pin from the geocoded centroid.

Japanese-language prize-draw gimmick built on a globe projection. dark-v11 style with projection: 'globe' and setFog atmosphere (space-color, star-intensity); demo-kit japanifyMap rewrites every symbol layer's text-field to a coalesce of name_ja and name. An idle requestAnimationFrame loop drives continuous easeTo rotation of the center longitude. Pressing the draw button runs a 2-second eased spin animation mutating center, zoom, pitch and bearing every frame, then fetches a prize tier from an external AWS API Gateway/Lambda endpoint (optional ?tier URL parameter forces a result; mock fallback data exists). On a winning tier it flashes a tier-themed setFog palette (gold/silver/bronze) then settles to a sustained one, builds a GeoJSON FeatureCollection of 30 randomly placed points, rasterizes three emoji onto 2D canvases and registers them with map.addImage, and adds a symbol layer whose icon-image is a match expression on the feature property. An animation loop ramps icon-size and icon-opacity via setLayoutProperty/setPaintProperty. DOM confetti elements are appended separately. Reset removes the layer and source and restores the original fog and camera.

Japanese-language click-to-trace map matching tool. streets-v12 map with the mapbox-gl-language plugin and NavigationControl, centered on Tokyo Station. Each map click pushes a coordinate, adds a numbered red Marker with a coordinate Popup, and extends a dashed GeoJSON LineString source of the raw clicks. Matching splits the coordinate list into segments wherever consecutive Turf distances exceed 50 m (simulated GPS dropout), further chunks each segment to 1000 points, and POSTs form-encoded coordinates/radiuses/timestamps/overview=full/tidy=false to the Map Matching API on a custom profile (mapbox.tmp.valhalla-zenrin) for driving, walking or cycling. Matched geometries become one FeatureCollection rendered as three stacked line layers — a blurred dark outline, a thick green line, and a dashed yellow accent — all with line-emissive-strength, then fitBounds. Radio-card profile picker, status box with distance/duration totals and failed-segment counts, GeoJSON file upload (Point, MultiPoint, LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon, GeometryCollection vertex extraction) and Blob download of current points. Layout follows the shared highway-sign.css template with its 380px #setup-panel that becomes a bottom sheet under 768px. Several Turf cleanup helpers (dedupe, jump filter, statistical outliers, simplify, DBSCAN) exist but are commented out.

Minimal third-party raster tile overlay demo, roughly 60 lines of script. A light-v11 map centered on Beijing at zoom 12 adds a raster source whose tiles array lists four AutoNavi/AMap subdomain URL templates using the {x}/{y}/{z} placeholders with tileSize 512 and a hardcoded AMap key. On load it walks map.getStyle().layers to find the first symbol layer id and inserts the raster layer directly beneath it, so Mapbox's own label symbols still draw on top of the foreign basemap imagery; paint sets raster-opacity 1 and raster-fade-duration 0. A commented-out block shows the alternative of adding the Mapbox Boundaries adm0 vector tileset (source-layer boundaries_admin_0) as a fill layer filtered to everything except iso_3166_1 = CN, masking the rest of the world. No controls, no popups, no UI panel, no interaction handlers.

Japanese merchant/store directory with a faceted sidebar filter over a vector tileset. light-v11 map (language ja) with NavigationControl, ScaleControl and FullscreenControl plus a live zoom/lat/lng badge updated on move and zoom. Data is the vector tileset mapbox://kenji-shima.merchants-z16 (source-layer merchants), drawn as a circle layer with minzoom 13 whose circle-color is a match expression over 24 numeric genre ids. Layout follows the shared storefront.css template with its 340px #directory-panel. Sidebar controls: debounced text search on the name property, a six-item color-coded category filter, a dependent genre filter that only reveals genres mapped to the selected categories, an independent brand filter (30 chains), and three perk toggles (coupon, campaign, points). buildFilterExpression composes an all expression from match filters on properties c, g and b, == checks on cp/cm/pt, and an in over downcase of n, applied with map.setFilter. Clicks queryRenderedFeatures and open a single tracked custom-styled Popup with category/genre/brand names and perk badges. Cluster tileset, cluster circle/label layers and layer toggles are present but commented out.

Threebox 3D character walking along a routed path while sampling Mapbox Probe Layer data. Standard style at pitch 60; a custom layer with renderingMode 3d hosts Threebox, which loads an FBX character and drives walk/idle clips through a THREE.AnimationMixer, with ground altitude calibrated by Newton iteration on foot-bone world z and the idle pose chosen by scanning the clip for the legs-together frame. Clicking sets start and destination markers and demo-kit setRoute fetches a walking Directions route (polyline geometry decoded to GeoJSON). Replay animates turf.along positions over a duration derived from turf.lineDistance, wipes a line-gradient over a lineMetrics GeoJSON source to reveal progress, rotates and setCoords the model, and drives a chase camera via getFreeCameraOptions/MercatorCoordinate/lookAtPoint on a time-based orbit, paused by raw canvas mousedown/touchstart/wheel listeners with a resume-follow button. Every 150 m it calls the Tilequery API on mapbox.mpl-v2-0-0 (radius 1609 m, limit 50) and appends returned features to a red circle layer; a category filter dropdown applies setFilter and clicks open a popup with type, class and density_rank. POI labels are hidden via setConfigProperty during the walk. Layout comes from the shared tarmac-glass.css template plus the light-preset-pill control.

Third-party address/door-point data QA viewer comparing a vendor dataset against Mapbox Geocoding. The map is constructed with bounds plus fitBoundsOptions rather than center/zoom, and gets a NavigationControl. A region dropdown (Japan, New Zealand, United States) drives a config object of per-region vector tileset URLs, bounds, language and evaluation-report link; switching a region removes and re-adds both sources and layers and fitBounds to the new extent. Two circle layers — Naurt doors (blue) and Naurt addresses (green) — each use a zoom-interpolated circle-radius and are toggled by checkboxes through setLayoutProperty visibility. Clicking either layer runs queryRenderedFeatures and opens a Popup that dumps every feature property into a table plus an async Geocoding v6 reverse call (longitude/latitude/language) whose full_address is written into the already-open popup element. A stats section renders match-rate percentage bars with color thresholds and links out to a per-region markdown evaluation report.

CSV trace viewer contrasting raw GPS fixes with Navigation SDK map-matched fixes. streets-v12 map with NavigationControl. Eight bundled sample CSVs under assets/navigation-trace are loaded by fetch, or a file is dropped/uploaded; the parser splits on commas for timestamp, lat, lng, type (raw or matched), recording flag, trip id and session id. Raw points render as a red circle layer, matched points as a green circle layer, and the matched sequence also as a thick green LineString layer, then fitBounds; a stats panel shows point counts, session duration and cumulative Turf distance, with toggle buttons flipping layer visibility. The distinctive part is a rectangle-selection repair mode: mousedown/mousemove/mouseup with dragPan disabled draw a polygon into a fill plus dashed-outline source, points inside are split into before/target/after, densified to 40 m spacing with turf.along, chunked and POSTed to the Map Matching API (mapbox.tmp.valhalla-zenrin driving) through a custom RateLimiter class (50 requests/second, 10 concurrent), and the returned geometry is spliced back into the route. A full-screen processing overlay covers parsing and matching.

Raster-array weather tileset explorer and styling sandbox. A dropdown of about 25 Mapbox tilesets (raster-array model output at several max zooms, raster satellite and smoke imagery, vector lightning and hotspot point sets) fully recreates the map on change; a second dropdown switches among eight projections via setProjection, and setFog supplies atmosphere. For raster-array tilesets it inspects source.rasterLayers to read each layer's name, band list and value range, then adds a raster layer in slot bottom whose raster-color is a step (or interpolate) expression over raster-value built either from d3 interpolators (Turbo, Spectral, Magma, Viridis, Cividis, Cubehelix and more) quantized to a selectable 8-256 color steps, or from hardcoded JMA sediment and Yahoo rain scales; raster-color-range, raster-resampling nearest and raster-array-band are set explicitly. A gradient legend bar is regenerated with 1-2-5 tick labels. A band timeline slider plus Play loop steps raster-array-band, with band values converted from days-since-1990 to Sydney-local timestamps. When a wind layer exists it adds a raster-particle layer with count, speed-factor and color controls. showTileBoundaries is on.

Aviation NOTAM proximity analysis, entirely client-computed from hardcoded arrays. Standard style with lightPreset set to night on style.load. Fifteen Singapore-hub routes (from/to pairs) become great-circle LineStrings via turf.greatCircle with 100 points; seven fictional NOTAMs (center, radius in nautical miles, type, altitude band, validity) become turf.circle polygons plus separate threshold-ring circles at the slider's current radius. turf.pointToLineDistance and turf.nearestPointOnLine in nauticalmiles classify each route/NOTAM pair as clear, alert or inside, and severity ranking picks the worst per route and nearest per NOTAM. Layers: route lines colored by a match on status, NOTAM fills plus outlines, dashed threshold-ring lines, dashed connector lines from each flagged NOTAM to its nearest point on a route with a symbol layer of distance labels, and NOTAM circle points — all using -emissive-strength paint properties. A range slider changes the alert threshold and re-renders every source. Scrollable panel lists routes and NOTAMs with status badges; clicking a route fitBounds it, clicking a NOTAM does a flyTo camera animation and opens a detail popup.

Indoor floorplan viewer with an exploded-floors 3D effect, structured as two subclasses of mapboxgl.Map that are torn down and recreated when switching modes. Map3D uses a custom Studio style and setConfigProperty calls for place/road/POI/transit label visibility and font. IndoorMap and RouteIndoorMap consume the mapbox.indoor-v1 vector tileset: for each of twelve floor ids (-7 to 4) they add line layers over indoor_floorplan and indoor_structure, two fill-extrusion layers (non-room floor plate and rooms, room color driven by a case expression on feature-state hover and selection), and a symbol layer over indoor_poi_label with maki icon-image coalesce and name_ja text. The exploded stacking comes from per-floor line-translate / fill-extrusion-translate / text-translate offsets recomputed from zoom and pitch on every zoom and pitch event, with non-active floors dimmed. Custom controls: a ButtonControl stack of floor buttons (B7 to 5F), a MapSwitchControl toggling 3D and indoor, and a hand-rolled SearchBoxControl hitting the Search Box API suggest and retrieve endpoints with proximity, session token and country=jp, then a flyTo camera animation plus a temporary Marker. Room clicks pick the nearest feature by turf.centerOfMass and easeTo it.

No-code POI map authoring and image-export template. A main streets-v12 map is paired with a second GL JS map as an inset overview minimap that follows the main map with jumpTo on every move at a user-adjustable zoom offset, and remembers its own pan offset when dragged. All state (title, optional saved camera view, POI array) lives in one object persisted to localStorage. POIs are added either by arming a click-to-place mode on the map or by typing latitude/longitude; each sidebar row edits color, a short label, marker style (numbered, teardrop pin, or airport icon) and order, deletes, or triggers a flyTo camera animation. Markers are custom DOM elements from demo-kit createTeardropMarkerEl with coordinate Popups, rebuilt wholesale on every state change alongside a legend overlay that mirrors the list. A preset dropdown loads hardcoded Sapporo configs each carrying its own camera; otherwise the camera auto-fits with turf.bbox plus fitBounds. Config saves and loads as JSON, and an export button captures only the map container (map, legend, minimap) to PNG or JPG through demo-kit downloadElementScreenshot, which uses navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia to grab the tab and crops the frame to the element's bounding rect.

Japanese weather timeline combined with POI search and routing. light-v11 mercator map. Four raster-array precipitation tilesets (nowcast, past 60 minutes, 1-6 hour and 7-15 hour forecast) are loaded through their TileJSON endpoints and their band lists merged into a single time-sorted unified timeline; one raster layer per tileset is added under airport-label and switching frames just toggles raster-opacity between layers and sets raster-array-band, with a step raster-color rain scale and a vertical legend. The timeline slider is augmented with generated nowcast/forecast zone shading, boundary marker, tick marks and JST time labels, plus prev/next/play-pause transport controls. The right panel calls the Search Box API suggest then retrieve (session token, proximity from geolocation, types=poi, country JP); every result gets an orange Marker, a Directions API call on a custom profile whose polyline geometry is decoded by a hand-written decoder and drawn as a route line layer, and two Tilequery API lookups of the raster value at that POI — current precipitation and the value in the band nearest the computed arrival timestamp. Hovering a result highlights its marker and route and refits bounds with dynamically computed padding.

Isochrone-driven point selection over a vector tileset. A light-v11 Japanese-language map renders mapbox://kenji-shima.elevators (source-layer elevators) as a circle layer with minzoom 5 whose circle-color is a match expression over ten single-letter values of a tp property. A category filter dropdown applies setFilter with an == expression on tp. The same point set is also fetched separately as a raw GeoJSON file so it can be analyzed client-side. A button calls demo-kit fetchIsochrone for mapbox/driving with a 20-minute contour around the current map center, adds the returned polygon as a translucent red fill layer inserted beneath the points layer, then runs turf.booleanPointInPolygon over every feature in the fetched GeoJSON, applies an in filter on the matching ids, and renders a scrollable list of those ids; clicking a list row opens a Popup containing a table of every property and highlights the row, and clicking a map point highlights the matching list row instead. A clear button removes the isochrone layer and source and resets the filter.

Navigation deviation and recovery workbench on streets-v12 centered on Melbourne. Two click modes: place start/end, then place the deviation point and the driver's current position. The main route comes either from the Directions API with steps=true or from the Map Matching API run over synthetic interpolated waypoints. Intersections are harvested from step.intersections, deduplicated by location and classified entry-only, exit-only or dual into three colored circle layers. The nearest exit-capable intersection to the click is found with turf.nearestPointOnLine. Candidate re-entry intersections ahead of the deviation are projected onto the route line, then ranked by the Directions Matrix API in batches of 24 destinations with sources=0 and duration/distance annotations. The deviation route and up to three dashed return-route options are requested from Directions with exclude point lists, truncated at the first turf.lineIntersect crossing with the main route using turf.lineSlice, and de-duplicated by requiring re-entry points at least 50 m apart. An options panel lists duration and distance per option and selecting one emphasizes that route's line-width, line-opacity and circle paint.

River network rendering with client-side dynamic label placement. A light-v11 Japanese-language map adds the vector tileset mapbox://kenji-shima.floodrisk-all (source-layer rivers) as a blue line layer inserted below the style's waterway-label layer. On both sourcedata (when the source finishes loading) and moveend it recomputes labels: queryRenderedFeatures groups the visible line features by their RIVERCODE property, flattens MultiLineString coordinate arrays, filters vertices to those inside map.getBounds(), builds a Turf lineString, finds the midpoint with turf.along at half of turf.length, then snaps that midpoint to the nearest actual vertex by turf.distance. The resulting points feed a GeoJSON source rendered as a symbol layer with text-field from the riverCode property, text-allow-overlap, a wide white halo and padding. A large commented-out block shows the alternative click interaction: pick the clicked river or the nearest one by turf.nearestPointOnLine, add a second filtered line layer highlighting that RIVERCODE in red, and open a Popup with the code.

Tabbed POI walkthrough over mapbox/streets-v12 with language en. Data is a hardcoded POIS array of five objects (id, name, type, lng, lat, color, icon) plus a separate city coordinate; no external fetch. Three header tab buttons map to a VIEWS object of camera presets and trigger a flyTo camera animation (center, zoom, pitch, bearing, duration 1800). POIs render as DOM mapboxgl.Marker elements built by createTeardropMarkerEl from shared/demo-kit.js (SVG teardrop pin carrying either a numeric label or an inline SVG glyph), each with a mapboxgl.Popup showing name, type label and coordinates. Marker visibility is toggled per tab by setting element.style.display, so tab 1 shows only the city pin, tab 2 all five, tab 3 medical only. An on-map legend overlay lists the POIs; clicking a row flies to zoom 14. A second non-interactive mapboxgl.Map acts as an inset minimap, synced on the main map move event via jumpTo at a fixed zoom offset of 3, projection mercator. A screenshot button calls downloadElementScreenshot from demo-kit, which uses getDisplayMedia to capture and save a PNG.

Simulated disaster advisory map for Singapore CBD on mapbox/dark-v11 with turf.js. Geometry is hardcoded GeoJSON lifted from the mapbox-streets-v8 tileset: a Singapore River water polygon used as the flood no-go zone, a wider buffered ring as the caution zone, and four real building footprints as shelters; hazmat hot and warm zones are turf.circle at 0.35 km and 0.65 km. Six geojson sources feed fill plus line layers per zone class, two line layers for evacuation routes filtered on an isNearest feature property (thick solid fastest versus thin line-dasharray alternates), a symbol layer of duration labels positioned at turf.along midpoints, and circle plus symbol marker layers. ROUTE_DATA is eight precomputed Mapbox Directions walking routes covering every hazard-to-shelter pair with distance and duration. Clicking a hazard zone shows its routes to all four shelters with the fastest starred; clicking a shelter shows routes to both hazards at equal priority. A situation-report side panel lists hazards and shelters with click and keyboard activation running a flyTo camera animation to zoom 15 plus a popup. A scrolling advisory ticker carries a Singapore-time clock via Intl.DateTimeFormat.

Raster overlay comparison centered on Taipei at zoom 6 over a custom Studio base style. On load it scans map.getStyle().layers for the first symbol layer with a text-field and uses that id as the beforeId insertion point. Two raster sources are added below labels: the mapbox://mapbox.satellite tileset at tileSize 512, and a Mapbox Raster Tiles API source whose tiles URL is api.mapbox.com/styles/v1/{user}/{styleId}/tiles/512/{z}/{x}/{y}@2x, i.e. a Studio vector style served as rendered raster tiles. Both raster layers use raster-opacity 1 and raster-fade-duration 300. A styled radio-button control switches between the two by flipping the visibility layout property. A projection dropdown offers mercator, globe, equalEarth, naturalEarth, winkelTripel, albers, lambertConformalConic and equirectangular, wired through wireProjectionSelector from shared/demo-kit.js, which calls map.setProjection on change. NavigationControl and FullscreenControl sit bottom-right. A map click handler logs queryRenderedFeatures results. Useful as a reference for raster-vs-raster layer switching and for consuming a style through the Raster Tiles API.

Companion list page to store-locator.html with no map and no Mapbox GL JS usage at all, despite loading the library and shared/demo-kit.js. It fetches data/skylark-stores.json, tolerating array or wrapped items/data/stores shapes, filters to records whose extra_fields new-store flag equals 1, and sorts by opening date descending. Rendering is a flat divided list paginated at ten per page: each row shows a formatted Japanese opening date, a brand icon image resolved from the record category code, the store name, an address line and a details pill, and numeric pagination buttons rebuild the page in place. Every row is an anchor that deep-links back to the map page as store-locator.html?lat=<lat>&lng=<lng>&zoom=15.00, which the locator parses to restore that view. A total-count line reports how many new stores matched. Relevant only as a structural reference for the list-plus-deep-link half of a store locator, or for URL-state handoff between a list page and a map page, not for any layer, source or camera work.

Side-by-side Google Maps JS API versus Mapbox GL JS comparison in a two-pane split grid styled by shared/templates/arena.css. The Google map is loaded by injecting the Maps JS script with a user-supplied API key persisted in localStorage; without a key that pane shows a placeholder. Camera state is synced bidirectionally behind an isSyncing reentrancy flag: Google changes push into Mapbox via jumpTo with zoom minus one, Mapbox move pushes into Google via setOptions with zoom plus one to compensate 512 versus 256 px tiles, mapping pitch to tilt and bearing to heading. The Mapbox pane uses a custom Studio style with dragRotate, pitchWithRotate and touchZoomRotate disabled, loads eight brand PNG icons through map.loadImage plus map.addImage, adds a canvas-drawn circular fallback image, then adds a geojson source and a symbol layer whose icon-image is a coalesce over a concat expression on the brand property. A header text input filters a store select populated from data/skylark-stores.json via a category-code to brand-name map; selecting a store recenters both maps (Mapbox 17, Google 18) and plots the brand marker on each. A zoom readout overlays the Mapbox pane.

Production-grade Japanese restaurant store locator on a custom Studio style with maxBounds around Japan, an auto-triggered GeolocateControl and a CSS-re-anchored NavigationControl. Data is data/skylark-stores.json mapped to GeoJSON with brand, amenity and parking flags plus pre-parsed prefecture and wardCity. Instead of clustering it uses zoom-tiered area aggregation: prefecture pills below z11 and ward/city pills to z12, each a DOM mapboxgl.Marker count pill at a centroid precomputed over the filtered dataset, then z12 and above individual symbol layers using brand icon-image from a concat expression, a parking P text layer, and duplicate selected-store layers for z-order with a requestAnimationFrame icon-size pulse. The sidebar offers Search Box API suggest and retrieve autocomplete with proximity and session tokens, brand filters, an AND/OR amenity filter, and a viewport-filtered list with proximity sort from the map center, progressive batch loading, and a nearest-store pointer when empty. Camera work is a flyTo camera animation on icon and list selection, easeTo on area-pill click, and fitBounds for Search Box bbox results and route previews. Popups compute open/closed status and offer walking and driving Directions API route previews drawn on a line layer. Filter and camera state round-trip through the URL query string; a ja/en toggle drives map.setLanguage.

The Mapbox Storytelling scrollytelling template. scrollama plus an intersection-observer polyfill drive scroll-linked chapters over a non-interactive mapbox/dark-v11 map. A single config object holds style, title, subtitle, footer, theme, showMarkers, inset and a chapters array; each chapter carries id, alignment (left, right, center, full), image, description, a location with center, zoom, pitch, bearing and optional flyTo speed and curve, a mapAnimation name, a rotateAnimation flag, a callback name, and onChapterEnter/onChapterExit arrays of layer opacity actions. All chapter DOM is generated from config at runtime. onStepEnter runs the named camera animation (flyTo by default), optionally a 30-second rotateTo of bearing plus 180 after moveend, moves a single mapboxgl.Marker, and applies setPaintProperty opacity plus transition per layer type using a layerTypes lookup. A second non-interactive inset map tracks the main map: each move rebuilds a bbox polygon from map.getBounds and feeds it into a fill and a line layer. An optional 3D terrain branch adds a raster-dem source, setTerrain with exaggeration 1.5 and a sky layer. transformRequest appends a pluginName query parameter to every request.

Minimal fill-extrusion styling demo over central Singapore (Marina Bay) on one custom Studio style at zoom 16.5, pitch 60, bearing -20, with antialias enabled. It adds no sources or layers of its own; instead it targets a single pre-existing style layer named building copy and mutates it live. An instrument-plate control panel exposes a color input and an opacity range slider that call map.setPaintProperty for fill-extrusion-color and fill-extrusion-opacity on every input event, with mono readouts of the current values. On load it seeds both controls from map.getPaintProperty, normalizing whatever CSS color string the style holds into a six-digit hex through a 1x1 canvas fill so it is acceptable to an HTML color input. Controls added are NavigationControl with visualizePitch true and FullscreenControl. Responsive: the plate docks to the bottom edge below 480 px, and the entrance animation is disabled under prefers-reduced-motion. Best used as a reference for driving an existing style layer's 3D extrusion paint properties from UI controls rather than for generating extrusion geometry.

Style preview and QA harness: it loads one custom Studio style centered on Tokyo at zoom 10, pitch 0, bearing 0 and exposes only camera state. Controls are NavigationControl and FullscreenControl top-right and a metric ScaleControl with maxWidth 200 bottom-right. A floating coordinate readout and an info panel refresh zoom, lat, lng, bearing and pitch on the move, zoom, rotate and pitch events. Five hardcoded preset buttons (Tokyo, New York, London, Paris, San Francisco) each run a flyTo camera animation with duration 2000 and essential true. Clicking anywhere opens a mapboxgl.Popup with the clicked lat/lng. On style.load it logs the style name, source keys, layer count and version; an error handler logs map errors. No sources, layers, data files or API calls beyond the style itself. Structurally distinctive and worth flagging: the file is a broken template render, with a complete nested html document (its own head, style, body and script) sitting inside an outer page shell after an escaped DOCTYPE paragraph, so only the inner document should be copied as a reference.

Mobile e-money transaction-history mock (Tailwind CDN, Font Awesome) with a map view. Data comes from an external Rurubu/JTB POI API: demo-kit getFirstAddress reverse-geocodes the hardcoded center through the Mapbox Search reverse endpoint, a JIS municipality code is matched from a hosted json, then four category queries are fetched in parallel and converted into a GeoJSON FeatureCollection whose features are dressed as fake transactions with random dates, times and amounts. A list view renders the transactions; a detail view renders a receipt plus a Mapbox Static Images API image, built as styles/v1/{style}/static/geojson(<url-encoded FeatureCollection>)/lng,lat,zoom,bearing,pitch/600x300, so the marker is an encoded GeoJSON overlay. The map view is created lazily, fitBounds over all transaction coordinates plus the user point, disables POI labels via setConfigProperty on basemap, and adds a geojson source with promoteId plus a circle layer and a symbol label layer; circle-radius, stroke-width and stroke-color use case expressions on feature-state selected. A horizontally snap-scrolling card carousel is two-way bound to the map: scroll-end sets feature-state on the centered card, clicking a circle scrollIntoView-centers its card. A route button calls the Directions API on the valhalla-zenrin walking profile with polyline geometry, decoded by demo-kit polyline.toGeoJSON, and draws it on a line layer.

Animated multi-leg world tour on a globe projection with a built-in route editor. The style is an inline style object that imports mapbox://styles/mapbox/standard with night lightPreset and POI/road labels off, plus four model sources and model layers (plane, train, car, ship glb) using model-type location-indicator, zoom-interpolated model-scale, and model-rotation plus model-translation driven by setFeatureState pitch, roll, bearing and z-elevation. A hardcoded destinations array of origin/destination/vehicle legs supplies the itinerary; each leg path is either a turf.greatCircle or a Catmull-Rom spline through user-placed control points, with a parabolic altitude profile for planes and antimeridian splitting into MultiLineString. Edit mode draws a dashed preview line layer per leg, click-to-add draggable control-point markers, right-click or long-press to delete, and drag-reorder, add, edit and delete of legs in the sidebar. Playback advances legs on requestAnimationFrame, fitBounds per leg with vehicle-specific pitch and duration, grows a trail line layer, and updates a route info panel and running distance counter, ending in a confetti completion modal. Search Box API suggest and retrieve power city autocomplete; Geocoding v6 reverse geocoding powers pick-on-map selection. Optional MediaRecorder recording composites the map canvas with a hand-drawn overlay canvas into a downloadable webm.

Full Navigation-SDK-style turn-by-turn navigation built on GL JS, split into two classes. GLJSLocationPuckController owns a DOM mapboxgl.Marker puck (SVG arrow, rotationAlignment and pitchAlignment map), validates raw GPS for impossible speeds, calls the Map Matching API (matching/v5) with a two-point trajectory and per-point radiuses, snaps to the matched geometry with turf.nearestPointOnLine, derives bearing from actual puck movement, and animates with a ported ConstantVelocityInterpolator over requestAnimationFrame; it also maintains red matched-coordinate and blue raw-GPS circle debug layers. TurnByTurnNavigation fetches Directions API routes with polyline6 (decoded in-page), steps, banner_instructions and voice_instructions, draws casing and line layers, watches geolocation with movement and accuracy filtering, applies profile-tuned off-route snap/confirm/reroute thresholds against raw GPS, debounces rerouting, advances steps, speaks via SpeechSynthesis with iOS voice priming, and follows with easeTo while detecting user camera interaction. A setup sheet takes departure and destination by text, map click, a pick-on-map banner or presets; profile and ja/en selects drive map.setLanguage and the Directions profile. Simulation mode replays route coordinates with turf.along interpolation plus play/pause and 0.25x to 10x speed. A debug panel counts Directions and Map Matching calls. The file is a broken template render with a nested html document inside an outer page shell.

Japan precipitation nowcast and forecast browser built on raster-array tilesets. A PrecipitationLayerHelper class walks 39 time steps across the slider domain, deduplicating them down to about 22 distinct raster-array sources, picking tileset ids by naming pattern (nowcast-r-{utc}-30m, -60m and forecast-{utc}-6h, -15h) and adding one raster layer per source with a step raster-color expression over a precipitation ramp, raster-color-range 0 to 200, raster-resampling nearest, raster-emissive-strength 1 and raster-array-band. A bottom time slider walks the band domain, cross-hiding layers by setting raster-opacity and swapping raster-array-band. Above zoom 15 it calls the Tilequery API on the active raster tileset to read the precipitation value under the map center, then drives map.setRain (zoom-interpolated density and intensity, droplet-size, distortion, vignette) and sets the Standard style lightPreset from the simulated hour; a batched multi-band tilequery feeds an ApexCharts precipitation bar chart. A scrolling panel of 27 Japanese cities shows per-city weather icons from tilequery results and on click runs a flyTo camera animation to zoom 15.5 pitch 75 followed by a 360-degree requestAnimationFrame bearing spin. A second non-interactive minimap tracks the main map with a red center dot, and Geocoding v6 reverse geocoding names the current area. Threebox glb model loading is present but commented out.

Raster-array wind visualization over Australia on mapbox/dark-v11 with mercator projection. On load it fetches the tileset TileJSON from api.mapbox.com/v4/{tileset}.json to read the wind_speed raster layer's band list and value range, and sizes the time slider from it. One raster-array source backs three raster layers: a single heatmap layer used for the instant and fade-in modes, plus heatmap-a and heatmap-b used for cross-fade, each with raster-color built as an interpolate linear ramp on raster-value from one of five named color scales (turbo, viridis, plasma, inferno, magma), raster-color-range from the tileset, raster-resampling linear and a raster-opacity-transition. A second raster-array source feeds a raster-particle layer exposing raster-particle-count, -speed-factor, -color, -max-speed, -fade-opacity-factor and -reset-rate-factor. Controls: heatmap show toggle and opacity slider, a transition-mode select (no fade, fade-in on one layer, cross-fade across two), a color scale select, and particle show, count, speed and color controls. A bottom slider plus a play button step bands on a one-second interval, converting band values (forecast seconds from a base time parsed out of the tileset name) into formatted UTC timestamps. Structurally the file is an otherwise-normal document preceded by a stray escaped-DOCTYPE paragraph.

Generic raster-array and vector tileset explorer, configured here with four BOM wind tilesets at zoom levels 4, 6, 8 and 10 over mapbox/satellite-v9. A tilesets config object drives everything: each entry names a tileset url, a type (raster-array, raster-array-particle, raster, vector), an optional map style, an insert-above layer id, a colorscale, and layer names; changing the tileset select tears down every layer and source, and when the style differs calls setStyle and rebuilds on style.load. For raster-array it fetches TileJSON, enumerates raster_layers, and builds a step or interpolate raster-color expression either from d3 scale interpolators (turbo, spectral, magma, plasma, inferno, greys, viridis, cividis, warm, cool, cubehelix) quantized by a color-steps selector from 8 to 256, or from hand-written JMA-style rain, snow, sediment and kikikuru hazard ramps, and renders a gradient legend bar. Particle layers use raster-particle with count, speed and color controls. Vector tilesets get circle, fill, line, or a flood-specific line layer using case and interpolate expressions on TYPE, FLOODRISK and FLOODFCST. Also present: an eight-option projection selector, a zoom selector, showTileBoundaries, a source load-time readout, map.queryRasterValue on mousemove into a hover popup, a band time slider with a play loop, and a Japanese kikikuru danger-level legend panel.

Side-by-side Mapbox Directions API routing comparison. Two mapboxgl.Map instances share one custom Studio style and are kept in sync by an epsilon-guarded, isSyncing-flagged jumpTo mirror of center, zoom, bearing and pitch. The left pane requests the mapbox/{profile} Directions profile, the right pane requests mapbox.tmp.valhalla-zenrin/{profile}, with driving-traffic routed to the -premium variant. Clicking either map sets origin A then destination B as DOM circle markers mirrored onto both maps; both routes are then fetched in parallel behind a fetchId generation guard and drawn as a casing line layer, a line layer and a symbol arrow layer whose icon is a white triangle rendered on a canvas and registered with map.addImage, using symbol-placement line, symbol-spacing 100, icon-size 0.6 and icon-rotation-alignment map. Each pane renders duration, distance, the leg via summary and a numbered turn-by-turn step list from the Directions steps. Controls: A/B click-mode buttons, a travel-mode select (driving, driving-traffic, cycling, walking), per-pane Avoid dropdowns mapping checkboxes to the exclude parameter (ferry, unpaved, toll, motorway), a Clear button, and a preset dropdown of hardcoded customer-complaint cases (wrong-way and no-entry reports) that fitBounds both maps and surfaces the complaint text in a banner.
